function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
To get detailed information for a specific interface on a network device, you can use one of the following methods depending on your environment and the device’s capabilities: | Method | Typical Commands / Endpoints | What it returns | When to use | |--------|------------------------------|-----------------|-------------| | **CLI (SSH/Telnet)** | `show interface `
`show interface detail`
`show running-config interface ` | Full interface description, status, MTU, duplex, speed, MAC address, counters, errors, and configuration | You have direct console/SSH access and want the most complete view. | | **SNMP** | OIDs: `IF-MIB::ifDescr`, `IF-MIB::ifType`, `IF-MIB::ifPhysAddress`, `IF-MIB::ifOperStatus`, `IF-MIB::ifInOctets`, `IF-MIB::ifOutOctets`, etc. | Structured data via SNMP GET/GETNEXT/GETBULK | You’re monitoring via SNMP or need machine‑readable data. | | **RESTCONF / NETCONF** | RESTCONF: `GET /restconf/data/interfaces/interface=`
NETCONF: `value` | XML/JSON representation of interface config and state | Your device supports RESTCONF/NETCONF and you prefer API integration. | | **Device‑specific APIs** | Example: Cisco ACI: `GET /api/node/class/fcIf.json?query-target-filter=eq(fcIf.name,"")` | JSON with interface attributes, operational status, and policy info | You’re working within a specific vendor ecosystem (ACI, Junos, Arista EOS, etc.). | ### Quick CLI example ```bash # Replace GigabitEthernet0/1 with your interface name show interface GigabitEthernet0/1 show interface GigabitEthernet0/1 detail show running-config interface GigabitEthernet0/1 ``` ### Quick SNMP example (using snmpwalk) ```bash snmpwalk -v2c -c public 192.168.1.1 IF-MIB::ifDescr snmpwalk -v2c -c public 192.168.1.1 IF-MIB::ifOperStatus ``` ### Quick RESTCONF example (using curl) ```bash curl -k -u admin:admin https://192.168.1.1/restconf/data/interfaces/interface=GigabitEthernet0%2F1 ``` Choose the method that best fits your device’s supported protocols and your automation stack.
